findings.title: Removing coarse lock from BuildIndex allows concurrent builds for the same key, risking file-based index corruption
findings.body: The previous code held `cacheMu.Lock()` for the entire `BuildIndex` function, which serialized all index builds. The new code only locks around the final cache write. This means two concurrent callers (e.g., a search request and a watch event handler both calling `getOrCreateIndex` for a namespace that wasn't pre-built during init) can simultaneously execute `BuildIndex` for the same key. When `size > b.opts.FileThreshold`, both goroutines will call `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` on the same directory path, which can corrupt the index or return errors. Even for memory-based indexes, duplicate work is performed and one index is silently discarded. A per-key lock or a singleflight/deduplication mechanism is needed to prevent concurrent builds for the same key.

findings.title: History and Origin methods will panic with nil pointer dereference when search is not configured
findings.body: `s.search.History(ctx, req)` and `s.search.Origin(ctx, req)` are called without checking whether `s.search` is nil. The `Search` method (line 916) correctly checks `if s.search == nil` before delegating, but `History` and `Origin` do not. If `opts.Search.Resources` is nil or `opts.Search.Backend` is nil (causing `newSearchSupport` to return nil), the server is created successfully but calling History or Origin will panic. The removed `Init` calls did not protect against this either, but since this PR is modifying these exact methods, it would be appropriate to add the nil check.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates over cache map without holding the read lock
findings.body: `TotalDocs()` ranges over `b.cache` without acquiring `b.cacheMu.RLock()`. Since `BuildIndex` now writes to `b.cache` under a brief lock (lines 137-139), there is a data race between a concurrent `BuildIndex` writing to the map and `TotalDocs` iterating it. This can cause a runtime panic ('concurrent map iteration and map write'). The `TotalDocs` method should acquire `b.cacheMu.RLock()` before iterating.

findings.title: Data race on totalBatchesIndexed incremented from multiple goroutines
findings.body: In `searchSupport.init()`, `totalBatchesIndexed` is a local `int` variable that is incremented (`totalBatchesIndexed++`) inside `group.Go` closures which run concurrently (up to `s.initWorkers` goroutines). This is a data race. It should be an `atomic.Int64` or the increment should be moved after `group.Wait()` by collecting results.

findings.title: NewResourceServer now blocks on full index build, changing startup behavior and contract
findings.body: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` which builds all search indexes synchronously before returning. For large deployments, this could significantly increase startup time and may exceed caller timeouts or health check deadlines. The PR description acknowledges this question ('Does anything else depend on initializing US lazily?') but there is no mechanism (e.g., a context with a configurable timeout, or an option to skip eager init) to control this behavior. Callers that previously had a fast `NewResourceServer` followed by lazy initialization may now experience startup failures if index building takes too long.
